answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit locked while it earns, so creating thousands of hollow shells costs real capital per shell. Rewards then flow only to identities whose work is attested by independent peers, and a public beacon, an on-chain registry of proven contributors, lets buyers check reputation before paying. An attacker chasing the nectar of rewards must fund every fake, pass peer attestation for each, and still appear on no trusted registry, so the cost of faking exceeds the payout.
